output:
PROBLEM STATEMENT:
A marketing operations manager reports that workbook exports beyond roughly 100,000 rows or 90 days of data crash the browser tab, so large reporting periods cannot be exported directly. Quarterly reporting now depends on manual slicing and conversion.

USER STORY:
As a marketing operations manager, I want a server-side export that completes reliably for large result sets, So that any report can be exported in full without browser crashes or manual stitching.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: Large export crashes workbook
Given a report whose result set exceeds 100,000 rows
When the user requests a spreadsheet export
Then the export is generated server-side and delivered complete within a documented time bound

input:
Raising this after another frustrating morning — I manage the permissions console for our org (compliance auditor at a financial services firm). Basically, API tokens are born with the creator's full permissions by default. We have hundreds of these tokens in CI systems.

Regards,
Ben O.
output:
PROBLEM STATEMENT:
A compliance auditor at a financial services firm reports that newly created API tokens inherit the creator's full permissions by default with no scope selection. A single leaked token from a CI system exposes everything its owner can access, which fails security review.

USER STORY:
As a compliance auditor at a financial services firm, I want scoped API tokens where permissions are selected explicitly at creation, So that machine credentials carry only the permissions their integration requires.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: API token defaults to owner permissions
Given a user creates a new API token
When the creation flow is completed
Then the token is issued with only the scopes explicitly selected during creation
And existing tokens can have their scopes narrowed without reissuance

input: I'm the operations director at a franchise group here and I look after the access management module. Basically, there's no control over guest-to-guest invitations. The setting to block it doesn't exist as far as we can tell. We've worked around it for now but it's not sustainable.

input: Raising this after another frustrating morning — I'm the solutions architect at a technology partner here and I look after the webhooks subsystem. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: Rate limit response omits retry-after header
Given a client exceeds its API rate limit
When the API returns a 429 response
Then the response includes Retry-After plus quota and reset headers

input: As the solutions architect at a technology partner, I spend a lot of time in the webhooks subsystem. Basically, when our endpoint is slow we get hit with an instant retry storm and events start dropping. There's no Retry-After to key off of. we built a polling fallback, doubling our API costs. Can we get this looked at before the next release?
output:
PROBLEM STATEMENT:
A solutions architect at a technology partner reports that webhook deliveries retry immediately with no exponential backoff, so a briefly slow consumer ends in dropped events. Downstream datasets silently undercount and consumers build costly polling fallbacks.

USER STORY:
As a solutions architect at a technology partner, I want webhook retries with exponential backoff and a documented dead-letter policy, So that temporarily unavailable endpoints never cause permanent event loss.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: Webhook events dropped during retry storm
Given a webhook consumer endpoint is temporarily unavailable
When delivery attempts fail
Then retries follow exponential backoff for at least 24 hours before the event is dead-lettered
